info.title: Scheduling Legacy API v1
info.description: Legacy v1 Platform API endpoints for scheduling domain including appointments, bookings, services, and availability

get.description:
## Overview
Retrieves a paginated list of appointments for the business. Supports filtering by client, appointment state, and sorting.

## Booking note
Appointments are the scheduled items on the business calendar. To **create** an appointment (and to handle client lifecycle actions such as reschedule/cancel), use the Bookings endpoints (for example: `POST /platform/v1/scheduling/bookings`).

Available for **Staff and Application tokens**.

parameters.name: business_id

parameters.description: Client ID Filter
parameters.name: client_id

parameters.description: State Filter - rejected/scheduled/done/cancelled/pending_reschedule/reschedule e.g state=done,rejected
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: Multiple order by option - updated:DESC,start_at:ASC,created:DESC
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: Page number of results. Default: 1
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: How many items to return per page. Default: 25. Max: 100
parameters.name: per_page

post.description:
## Overview
Creates a booking for either an appointment with a staff member or registration for a group event.

## Relationship to appointments and events
A **booking** is the lifecycle/action interface for scheduled items:
- For an **appointment booking**, this endpoint creates the appointment on the business calendar and returns it as a `booking` object.
- For an **event registration**, this endpoint creates a registration (attendance) for the event instance and returns it as a `booking` object.

## When to use
If you are looking for an endpoint to **create appointments** or **register clients to events**, this is the endpoint to use.

## Authentication
Available for **Client and Staff tokens**. The endpoint also accepts **unauthenticated** requests, which is how anonymous client-portal / LiveSite bookings are created: when no token is supplied, the client is resolved (or created) from the email in `form_data.fields`.

Supply a Client token together with `client_id` to book on behalf of an existing, known client.

## Required fields
`business_id` is always required. For an **appointment** booking, `service_id`, `staff_id`, `start_time` and `form_data` are required as well. For an **event registration**, supply `event_instance_id` and `form_data` instead of `service_id` / `staff_id` / `start_time`.

A missing top-level parameter fails with `400 PARAMETER_MISSING`; a missing scheduling-form field fails with `422 FORM_VALIDATION_ERROR`.

## Prerequisites
- `service_id` and the staff uids that may provide it (`providers_staff`) come from `GET /platform/v1/services`.
- A bookable `start_time` comes from `GET /platform/v1/staff/availability`. **Availability slots are returned at a fixed granularity (10 minutes) regardless of the service duration** - you must verify that the full service duration fits in a contiguous run of returned slots, otherwise the booking fails with `422 TIMESLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.
- The `form_data.fields` uids come from `GET /platform/v1/scheduling/scheduling_forms/get_form`.

client_id.description: Client uid. Only usable with a Client token. Does not exempt the request from scheduling-form validation: fields marked `required: true` must still be supplied via `form_data.fields`, otherwise the request fails with 422 `FORM_VALIDATION_ERROR`.

event_instance_id.description: Event instance uid. Required for event registration (not appointment booking).

fields.description: Client fields, keyed by field uid. Values are strings, except a phone field which takes an object (e.g., {"prefix_value": "US", "value": "5551234"}).

service_fields.description: Service-specific custom fields, keyed by fieldset field id. Omit when the service has no fieldset.

meeting_details.description: Meeting location details. Required when the service interaction_type is client_location or client_phone.

meeting_interaction_details.description: Location or contact details for the meeting

policies.description: Policy acceptance, keyed by policy id (e.g., {"meetings_policy": true}).

portal_id.description: Business uid (same as business_id, for portal context)

service_id.description: Service uid. Required for appointment booking.

staff_id.description: Staff uid. Required for appointment booking. Must be one of the service's `providers_staff` (see `GET /platform/v1/services`).

start_time.description: ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-09-16T15:00:00Z"). Required for appointment. Must be a slot where the whole service duration fits - see `GET /platform/v1/staff/availability`.

time_zone.description: Default is set to UTC if not provided

booking.title: In-office appointment
booking.auto_reply_message: Thanks for your booking. Looking forward to meeting you!

400.description: A mandatory top-level parameter is missing. `error` is a string.

422.description: Business-rule failure. Note that the type of `error` depends on `error_code`: it is a **string** for `TIMESLOT_UNAVAILABLE` / `ALREADY_REGISTERED`, and an **object keyed by scheduling-form field uid** for `FORM_VALIDATION_ERROR`.

Booking (appointment/event) uid. Can be obtained from:

put.description:
## Overview
Update RSVP state for a booking. Available for **Client tokens** only.

## Required Parameters
- `booking_uid` (path): The booking UID
- `new_rsvp_state` (query): Valid values: 'confirmed', 'cancelled', 'pending'
- `appointment_type` (body): 'appointment', 'event_instance', or 'event_attendance'
- `business_id` (body): The business UID

parameters.description: Booking UID
parameters.name: booking_uid

parameters.description: New RSVP State. 'confirmed' is the only valid option. any other state is forbidden (return 403)
parameters.name: new_rsvp_state

get.description:
## Overview
Get Event attendance details for a specific event attendance record.

## Booking note
To **register a client** to an event instance, create a booking using `POST /platform/v1/scheduling/bookings` and provide `event_instance_id`.

Available for **Staff and App tokens**.

## Notes
- The event attendance UID can be obtained from the event attendance creation response (POST to `/v2/event_instances/{event_instance_id}/event_attendances`) or from the event instance details.
- Previously documented under `/api/v2/event_instances/{event_instance_id}/event_attendances/{id}`, but that v2 nested route does not have a working `show` action. The correct route is `/platform/v1/scheduling/event_attendances/{event_attendance_uid}`.

parameters.description: Event attendance UID. Obtain from event attendance creation response or event instance attendees list (e.g., `$.data.event_attendance.uid`).
parameters.name: event_attendance_uid

get.description:
## Overview
Returns the definition of the business's **scheduling form** - the fields a client must fill in when booking.

## Why you need it
The field uids returned here are the keys of `form_data.fields` in `POST /platform/v1/scheduling/bookings`. Every field with `required: true` must be present in `form_data.fields`, otherwise the booking fails with `422 FORM_VALIDATION_ERROR`. There is no fixed set of uids - they differ per business, so this endpoint must be called before booking.

## Structure
`data.sections` is an array of sections. A section of `type: "fields"` carries `fields` as an **array of arrays** (rows of fields); a section of `type: "policies"` carries policy entries whose `id` (e.g. `meetings_policy`) is the key used in `form_data.policies`.

Accessible **without authentication**, as well as with Client, Staff and Directory tokens.

parameters.description: Business uid
parameters.name: business_id

post.description:
## Overview
Join an event waitlist.

## Booking note
To **register a client** directly to an event instance (instead of joining the waitlist), create a booking using `POST /platform/v1/scheduling/bookings` and provide `event_instance_id`.

Available for **Staff, App, Directory, and Client tokens**.

## Client Identification
Client tokens: The client is identified from the token.
Staff/App/Directory tokens: Must provide `client_id` to identify which client to add to the waitlist.

## Note
Validation errors may return dynamic form field IDs. To get the form field definitions, call `GET /platform/v1/forms?business_id={business_id}&form_type=scheduling&service_uid={event_service_id}`.

client_id.description: Client UID. Required for Staff/App/Directory tokens.

event_instance_id.description: Event instance UID. Required - identifies which event to join the waitlist for.

matter_uid.description: Matter/conversation UID to associate with this waitlist entry.

time_zone.description: Time zone for the waitlist entry.

put.description:
## Overview
Cancel a waitlist registration.

## Booking note
To **register a client** to an event instance (instead of joining a waitlist), create a booking using `POST /platform/v1/scheduling/bookings` and provide `event_instance_id`.

Available for **Client tokens**.

The underlying controller inherits from `Api::ClientApi::V1::BaseController`, which only accepts client authentication.

## Required Fields
- **Always required**: `business_uid`, `event_instance_uid`, `client_uid`, and `matter_uid`
- `client_uid` must be explicitly provided in the request body for the authorization check to pass. The controller extracts it from the request parameters, not from the token.
- `matter_uid` is used to look up the specific waitlist entry to cancel.

## Note
Staff can cancel waitlist entries using the business API endpoint `PUT /business/scheduling/v1/waitlist/cancel` which supports staff tokens and the `waitlist_uid` parameter.

client_uid.description: Client UID. Required. Must be explicitly provided in the request body for the authorization check (`authorize_action(:cancel_waitlist)`) to pass. The controller reads this from `params[:client_uid]`, not from the token.

event_instance_uid.description: Event instance UID. Required. Identifies which event's waitlist to cancel from.

matter_uid.description: Matter/conversation UID. Required. Used to look up the specific waitlist entry to cancel.

get.description:
## Overview
Lists the bookable services of a business - both `AppointmentService` (one-on-one appointments) and `EventService` (group events).

## Why you need it
This is where `service_id` for `POST /platform/v1/scheduling/bookings` comes from, together with `providers_staff` - the staff uids allowed to provide that service, which is what you pass as `staff_id`.

Two service attributes change what the booking request must contain:
- `interaction_type` - when it is `client_location` or `client_phone`, `form_data.meeting_details.meeting_interaction_details` is required.
- `duration` - determines how many consecutive slots from `GET /platform/v1/staff/availability` the booking needs.

Accessible **without authentication**, as well as with Client, Staff and Directory tokens.

parameters.description: Business uid
parameters.name: business_id

get.description:
## Overview
Returns available time slots for one or more staff members. The endpoint considers staff weekly availability schedules, calendar sync conflicts, blocked times, and existing bookings to compute open appointment or event slots.

The response can be aggregated by date (default) or by staff member using the `aggregate_by` parameter.

Authentication is optional. When a valid client token is provided, availability may be filtered based on the client's context. When no token is provided, the endpoint returns availability without client-specific filtering.

Available for **Staff, Directory, and Client tokens**. Also accessible without authentication.

## Slot granularity
Slots are returned at a fixed granularity (10 minutes), **independent of the duration of the service you intend to book**. A returned slot start is therefore not by itself a bookable start time: to book a 60-minute service you must confirm that six consecutive 10-minute slots are present with no gap. Booking a start time whose service duration does not fit fails with `422 TIMESLOT_UNAVAILABLE` on `POST /platform/v1/scheduling/bookings`.

parameters.description: The start date of the availability window in `YYYY-MM-DD` format (e.g., "2026-03-03"). Must be a valid date string that can be parsed into a timezone-aware datetime.
parameters.name: start_date

parameters.description: The end date of the availability window in `YYYY-MM-DD` format (e.g., "2026-03-10"). Must be a valid date string that can be parsed into a timezone-aware datetime. The range between `start_date` and `end_date` determines the window for which availability slots are returned.
parameters.name: end_date

parameters.description: Comma-separated list of staff member UIDs to query availability for (e.g., "j9c1xh0vzvkr2g0g" or "j9c1xh0vzvkr2g0g, abc123def456"). If the value is a comma-separated string, it will be split into an array internally. At least one staff UID should be provided for meaningful results.
parameters.name: staff_ids_array

parameters.description: Business uid. Although the endpoint returns `200 OK` without it, the response is then an **empty** `availabilities` object with no error - in practice this parameter is required for any meaningful result.
parameters.name: business_id

parameters.description: IANA time zone identifier used to localize the returned availability slots (e.g., "UTC", "America/New_York", "Asia/Jerusalem"). Defaults to "UTC" if not provided. The time zone affects the `start_time` formatting and date grouping in the response.
parameters.name: time_zone

parameters.description: Controls how the availability slots are grouped in the response. When set to "date" (the default), slots are grouped by date string (e.g., "2026-03-03"). When set to "staff", slots are grouped first by staff UID and then by date, and the `staff_id` field is removed from individual slot objects.
parameters.name: aggregate_by

parameters.description: An existing booking instance UID to exclude from the availability calculation. This is useful when rescheduling an appointment — the time currently occupied by this booking will be treated as available. (e.g., "bk_abc123")
parameters.name: booking_instance_id

parameters.description: When set to "true", the returned `start_time` values will include daylight saving time (DST) offset adjustments for the specified time zone. When "false" or omitted, DST adjustments may not be applied.
parameters.name: include_dst

parameters.description: When set to "true", includes availability slots that fall before the current time. By default ("false"), only future availability is returned.
parameters.name: show_past_availabilities

parameters.description: When set to "true", ignores the business's minimum scheduling notice (the minimum amount of time before an appointment can be booked). Useful for internal tools or admin-level booking where the minimum lead time should not apply.
parameters.name: ignore_min_schedule

parameters.description: The type of service to check availability for. "AppointmentService" returns individual appointment slots based on staff schedules. "EventService" returns event instance availability with additional fields such as pricing and interaction details.
parameters.name: type

200.description: Availability slots retrieved successfully. The structure of `availabilities` depends on the `aggregate_by` parameter.

400.description: Bad Request - A required parameter is missing.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity - The request parameters are invalid (e.g., invalid date range or time zone).

x-response-aggregate-by-staff.description: When aggregate_by=staff, the availabilities object is keyed by staff UID instead of date. Each staff UID maps to an object of dates, each containing an array of slots. The staff_id field is removed from individual slot objects in this mode.

Bearer.description: Provide a valid bearer token in the Authorization header. Example: 'Authorization: Bearer {app_token}'
